sentences.text: Jiangjunosaurus was a medium-sized, herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur that lived in the Junggar Basin of Xinjiang, China.
This armored dinosaur reached lengths of 6 to 7 meters and weighed approximately 2.5 metric tons, though some estimates suggest a mass of 1,500 kilograms.
The species is distinguished by symmetrical tooth crowns that are wider than tall, a rectangular profile on the spine of the axis vertebra, and large vein openings in the rear neck vertebrae.
Its lower jaws feature a predentary bone with a deep, hook-shaped chin.
A significant gap exists between this chin bone and the row of teeth, measuring about four tooth positions in width.
A vertical plate extends upward from the rear of a bone shelf on the outside of the tooth row, obscuring the teeth in side view, while the front and back teeth completely lack vertical ridges.
The axis, the second neck vertebra, possesses a unique rectangular profile in side view instead of the typical triangular shape found in other dinosaurs.
CAT scans revealed that the large openings in the rear neck vertebrae were not connected to inner air spaces but probably served as vein channels.
Two neck plates have been preserved in the fossil record, likely in their original position on the animal's back.
Liu Yongfei discovered the remains of a stegosaurian in 2002.
The holotype specimen IVPP V 14724 was found in the Shishugou Formation, located in the Xinjiang Province of China.
The elements of the holotype were found in almost perfect articulation, representing a subadult individual.
The genus Jiangjunosaurus was described by Jia et al. in 2007 based on the front half of a subadult skeleton.
The generic name Jiangjunosaurus refers to the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao, an ancient desert city named after a general's burial temple.
The species name refers to the Junggar region where the fossils were found.
It is suggested that Jiangjunosaurus may have been prey for the dinosaur Sinraptor.
Jiangjunosaurus belongs to the suborder Stegosauria and the family Stegosauridae.
The dinosaur was placed in the family Stegosauridae in 2007.
Researchers concluded that Jiangjunosaurus held a basal position within the Stegosauridae.
This basal classification was based on comparative anatomy rather than an exact cladistic analysis.
Jiangjunosaurus lived during the late Jurassic, approximately 162 to 156 million years ago, specifically during the Oxfordian stage between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
